dedupe_keys.name: itu national emergency telecommunication plans netps guidelines and regional frameworks

description: The ITU National Emergency Telecommunication Plans page gathers the plans, guidelines and model frameworks with which countries organise telecommunications before, during and after disasters. A NETP sets out the regulatory framework for disaster risk management, maps of the hazards a country faces, the landscape of operators, facilities and service penetration, standard operating procedures, response and contingency plans, and the international agreements that apply, such as the Tampere Convention. The page states that an ITU assessment of 100 countries, mainly in the Americas, Arab States and Pacific Islands, found about 63 per cent had or were developing a plan; that as of August 2026 ITU had helped develop 44 NETPs, 13 in least developed countries, 12 in small island states and 11 in landlocked developing countries; and that it was supporting eight more, including Bangladesh, Pakistan and South Sudan. It also offers two regional frameworks, for the Southern African Development Community and for West Africa, each covering 16 countries, the ITU Guidelines for national emergency telecommunication plans, a guide to national emergency roaming, free e-courses and news of plans handed over, for example in Haiti and Senegal in 2026. Coverage: global programme with country plans mostly in developing countries. Format and access: web pages and PDF documents, free. Caveats: not every country plan is published, and plans are policy documents, not data. Simulation uses: emergency communication procedures and roles for response scenarios, and baselines for telecom resilience planning. Related records: the Tonga cable cut case shows why such plans matter.
